payload.task_text:
The e-commerce manager wants a monthly sales performance presentation to share with stakeholders and needs a planning meeting scheduled. Analyze WooCommerce order data broken down by month to compute monthly revenue totals and order counts across all order statuses.

Create a PowerPoint presentation called Monthly_Sales_Review.pptx with the following slides. Slide 1 should be a title slide with "Monthly Sales Performance Review" as the title. Slide 2 should be titled "Monthly Revenue Overview" and contain a table showing each month (January through December), the number of orders, and the total revenue for that month. Slide 3 should be titled "Order Volume Trends" and describe the monthly order volume patterns. Slide 4 should be titled "Key Insights" and highlight the peak revenue month, the lowest revenue month, and total annual revenue. Slide 5 should be titled "Next Steps" with planned actions for improving sales performance.

Schedule a Google Calendar event called "Monthly Sales Review" on 2026-04-15 from 14:00 to 15:00 with a description noting it is a stakeholder review of monthly sales performance.

Email the presentation to ecommerce_manager@store.com with subject "Monthly Sales Performance Review" and include the key revenue highlights in the email body.

Task-Solving Rationable with Sub-task Decomposition:
To solve this task efficiently, complete it directly in the main agent and dispatch no sub-agent. The complete order catalog, twelve monthly rows, five-slide deck, one fixed meeting, and one email form one compact workflow.

Resolve the workspace dynamically. Start the independent meeting inventory and order retrieval in the same response: call `list_events(timeMin="2026-04-15T00:00:00", timeMax="2026-04-16T00:00:00", maxResults=100, orderBy="startTime")`, and call `woo_orders_list(perPage=100,page=1)` without `status`. Continue increasing order pages until a short or empty page, preserving all observed statuses; do not query by status/month and do not modify orders. Parse every observed order date and numeric total once, aggregate January through December counts and revenue including zero months, and freeze peak month, lowest month, and annual revenue with deterministic source-order tie handling.

Create `Monthly_Sales_Review.pptx` exactly once with one presentation ID and exactly the five requested slides, including all twelve monthly rows and insights derived only from the frozen table; read back the full slide inventory and verify every title/value. Filter the event inventory locally to exact `Monthly Sales Review` at 14:00–15:00, create once only if missing with exact `start.dateTime`/`end.dateTime` and description, retain the created/reused ID, and call `get_event`. Only after deck and event readback, check Sent mail for the exact recipient/subject; send one missing email with verified highlights and the presentation in the supported workspace-path `attachments` list, never retry an ambiguous send, and read back the attachment record before `claim_done`.

nodes.text:
You are analyzing WooCommerce order data for an e-commerce monthly sales review. You have read-only access to the WooCommerce MCP server via the `mcp__woocommerce__woo_orders_list` tool (use perPage=100 and iterate `page` until you have ALL orders; the store has ~128 orders total, so this should take about 2 pages).

GOAL: Produce a per-calendar-month aggregation of ALL orders, across ALL order statuses (completed, pending, on-hold, processing, cancelled, refunded, failed, etc.). Include every order — do not filter by status.

For each order, extract:
- `date_created` (ISO timestamp, e.g. "2025-12-01T23:02:37.781Z")
- `status`
- `total` (numeric, e.g. "98.95")

Group by calendar MONTH (the month portion of date_created). For each month report:
- month name
- number of orders
- total revenue (sum of `total`, rounded to 2 decimals)

Do this by consuming the paginated order lists. Use the filesystem `mcp__filesystem__read_text_file` on any saved tool-output JSON if that is more reliable than re-reading via the tool, and parse the JSON with Python (you have `mcp__local__python_execute`) to compute the sums precisely. Do NOT trust manual reading of numbers — compute them programmatically.

Also report:
1. The full year range covered by the data (min and max year present in date_created across all orders), and whether orders span multiple years.
2. The month with the highest total revenue (peak month) and its revenue.
3. The month with the lowest total revenue and its revenue.
4. The total annual revenue (sum of all order totals) and total order count.
5. If the data spans more than one year, ALSO produce a separate per-year monthly table (e.g. 2025 Jan–Dec and 2026 Jan–Dec) so the overall pattern is clear, plus which year each month belongs to.

RETURN (this is your contract — return exactly these in your final message):
- A clean monthly aggregation table: for each calendar month January–December, the order count and total revenue. If months span multiple years, clarify and provide both the all-data monthly totals AND the per-year breakdown.
- Peak revenue month + value, lowest revenue month + value.
- Total annual revenue and total order count.
- The year(s) represented in the data.
Push any full JSON to files under /workspace/dumps/kimi-code_claude-sonnet-5/SingleUserTurn-wc-order-monthly-ppt-gcal/workspace if needed; keep your final text message focused on the aggregated results.
Aggregate monthly WooCommerce orders

Build a PowerPoint presentation file at:
/workspace/dumps/kimi-code_[REDACTED]/SingleUserTurn-wc-order-monthly-ppt-gcal/workspace/Monthly_Sales_Review.pptx

Use the mcp__pptx__ tools. Here is the exact data and slide specifications:

---
MONTHLY DATA (2025 calendar year, all order statuses):
| Month     | Orders | Revenue ($)  |
|-----------|--------|-------------|
| January   |   0    |    0.00     |
| February  |   0    |    0.00     |
| March     |  12    | 1,636.15    |
| April     |   9    | 4,349.71    |
| May       |  10    | 6,023.29    |
| June      |  11    | 9,555.69    |
| July      |   8    | 3,921.19    |
| August    |  17    | 3,873.37    |
| September |  17    | 5,842.43    |
| October   |  11    | 4,447.76    |
| November  |  10    | 1,237.61    |
| December  |  17    | 8,843.75    |

2025 Annual totals: 122 orders, $49,730.95 total revenue
(Note: An additional 28 orders in Jan–Mar 2026 bring all-time totals to 150 orders / $61,712.04)
Peak month: June 2025 — $9,555.69 (11 orders)
Lowest month: November 2025 — $1,237.61 (10 orders)
---

SLIDE SPECIFICATIONS (5 slides):

SLIDE 1 — Title slide
- Title: "Monthly Sales Performance Review"
- Subtitle: "2025 Annual Overview | All Order Statuses"

SLIDE 2 — "Monthly Revenue Overview"
- Title: "Monthly Revenue Overview"
- A table with 13 rows (header + 12 months) and 3 columns: Month, Orders, Total Revenue
- Use exact values from the table above
- Format revenue values as dollar amounts (e.g., $9,555.69)

SLIDE 3 — "Order Volume Trends"
- Title: "Order Volume Trends"
- Bullet content describing patterns:
  • Business started gaining traction from March 2025 onward
  • Order volume peaked in August, September, and December at 17 orders each
  • Summer months (Jun–Aug) saw sustained high volume; fall months (Sep–Oct) remained strong
  • November saw a seasonal dip with only 10 orders — the lowest count among active months
  • December rebounded strongly with 17 orders, reflecting year-end buying activity
  • January and February had no recorded orders, suggesting the store launched in March 2025

SLIDE 4 — "Key Insights"
- Title: "Key Insights"
- Bullet content:
  • Peak Revenue Month: June 2025 — $9,555.69 across 11 orders
  • Lowest Revenue Month: November 2025 — $1,237.61 across 10 orders
  • Highest Order Volume Months: August, September, and December — 17 orders each
  • Total 2025 Annual Revenue: $49,730.95 across 122 orders
  • Revenue Recovery: December bounced back 614% from November's trough
  • Average Monthly Revenue (active months): ~$4,975 across 10 active months

SLIDE 5 — "Next Steps"
- Title: "Next Steps"
- Bullet content:
  • Launch targeted promotions in November to counteract seasonal revenue dip
  • Replicate June's high-revenue strategy (product mix, promotions) in slower months
  • Investigate why January and February had zero orders — evaluate early-year launch campaigns
  • Capitalize on December momentum with early January re-engagement campaigns
  • Set monthly revenue targets based on 2025 baseline; aim for $6,000+ average monthly revenue
  • Expand product catalog in high-demand months (Aug, Sep, Dec) to increase average order value

---

INSTRUCTIONS:
1. Call mcp__pptx__create_presentation to create a new presentation.
2. Build each slide using mcp__pptx__add_slide, mcp__pptx__populate_placeholder, mcp__pptx__add_table, mcp__pptx__add_bullet_points, and mcp__pptx__manage_text as appropriate.
3. Use color scheme "modern_blue" for all slides.
4. For the table on slide 2, use add_table with header_row=true, appropriate dimensions.
5. Save the final file to the path above using mcp__pptx__save_presentation.
6. Return: the full absolute path of the saved file, and confirmation that all 5 slides were created.
Build Monthly Sales Review PPTX

Create a Google Calendar event with the following details using the mcp__google_calendar__create_event tool:

- Summary (title): "Monthly Sales Review"
- Start: 2026-04-15T14:00:00 (timezone: America/New_York)
- End: 2026-04-15T15:00:00 (timezone: America/New_York)
- Description: "Stakeholder review of monthly sales performance. Agenda: review of 2025 annual sales data, monthly revenue trends, key insights, and next steps for improving sales performance."

After creating the event, return the event ID and a confirmation that it was created successfully.
Create Google Calendar event for sales review
